deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a cut-down library loan slip (Ausleihzettel), very likely from the Göttingen University Library. It records a request or loan of a periodical volume.

1. Top line, in brown ink: 'Mémoires de la Société [royale] des sciences de Liège. Tome VII. 1851'. This is the requested volume. 'Tome VII. 1851' is underlined in pencil.
2. Large blue-grey pencil numeral '8'. This is probably a librarian's shelf, loan or sequence number. It is not mathematical content.
3. Lower left, in red ink: 'Oct. 30. 52.' This is the loan or processing date, 30 October 1852.
4. Lower right, in Riemann's hand: 'B Riemann, Dr. ph.', followed by a parenthetical line. The parenthetical is probably his Göttingen address or lodging; it is hard to read.
5. Small pencil '48' at upper right: the archival folio number.

What the slip documents: on 30 October 1852 Riemann (then Dr. phil., Habilitand) borrowed or requested vol. VII (1851) of the Liège Society's Mémoires. The date falls in the period when he was writing his Habilitationsschrift on trigonometric series. It precedes his trial lecture of June 1854. So the slip is a small datum on his reading. I cannot say for certain which paper in that volume he wanted, and I do not attribute any specific article.

There is no derivation to reconstruct. The previous page is absent. The next page appears to be a dedication or gift note ('geschenkt … Hannover') and is unrelated mathematically.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an administrative library slip with no mathematical content. It is only of minor biographical interest as evidence of what Riemann was reading in autumn 1852, while working on the trigonometric-series Habilitationsschrift.
transcription_corrections: The page number '48' is the archival folio number written in pencil at the upper right edge; it is not part of the document text.
The large '8' is a pencil librarian's mark, not a mathematical symbol.
The date line is in red ink and reads 'Oct. 30. 52.' (30 October 1852).
The parenthetical under 'B Riemann, Dr. ph.' is not reliably 'Grossherzogl. Regel'. It is most likely a street or lodging address in Göttingen, and the reading remains uncertain.
The full name of the society is 'Société royale des sciences de Liège'; the slip omits 'royale'.
